# Caddy — root-to-custom-context-servlet-mapping

Proxy at /ui/, app on /app context with VAADIN_URL_MAPPING=/ui/*. The Hilla paths lose the servlet mapping and gain the context prefix; everything else only gains /app. The two rules sit in a route block because a Caddyfile runs directives in Caddy's fixed order, not as written, and that order puts rewrite before uri: written flat, the Hilla matcher never sees the path it was meant for.

Proxy URL on `http://localhost:9090`: `/ui/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

Caddy site block (`caddy/http/root-to-custom-context-servlet-mapping/vaadin.caddyfile`), mounted as
`/etc/caddy/vaadin.caddyfile`:

```caddyfile
# Proxy at /ui/, app on the /app context with VAADIN_URL_MAPPING=/ui/*.
#
# The Hilla paths lose the servlet mapping and gain the context prefix
# (/ui/HILLA/x -> /app/HILLA/x); everything else only gains /app. See
# vaadin/hilla#289.
#
# The route block is load-bearing. A Caddyfile does not run directives in the
# order they are written but in Caddy's own fixed directive order, and in that
# order `rewrite` comes before `uri`. Written out flat, the /app prefix would be
# added first, the @hilla matcher would then look at /app/ui/HILLA/... and never
# match. Every Hilla call then goes to /app/ui/connect/... instead of
# /app/connect/...: measured, HelloHillaIT fails while the Flow views keep
# working. Inside `route` the directives run as written.
:80 {
	import common

	@hilla path /ui/HILLA/* /ui/connect/*
	route {
		uri @hilla strip_prefix /ui
		rewrite * /app{uri}
	}

	reverse_proxy vaadin:8080 {
		header_down Location ^(https?://[^/]+)?/app(/.*)$ $1$2
		header_down Set-Cookie ^(.*;\s*[Pp]ath=)/app(;.*)?$ $1/$2
	}
}
```

The global options and the `common` snippet this file imports (the
access log and the compression allowlist) come from the shared
[Caddyfile](../../Caddyfile), mounted read-only over the image's own
`/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`. It imports this file, so the two only load as a pair.
